body: MAINLINE-035 filed. The measured record: the SBKF 8 ft honeycomb-core composite cylinders reached 0.721 to 0.87 of the shear-inclusive linear eigenvalue, at Vc 0.32 to 0.53 (my lamination arithmetic) and R/rho 335 to 413, which is 1.29 to 1.56 times SP-8007. The pre-1969 sandwich cylinders in CR-1457 Fig. 4.2-3 sit near SP-8007, at 0.42 to 0.76; FPL 1830 reads 0.42 and 0.44 at R/rho 1050 and 1300. The only measured sandwich domes are Saturn S-II, in CR-1457 Fig. 6.2-3, which I read from the page: two hemispheres at 0.22 to 0.24 (R/rho about 240, Vc unrecoverable) and ellipsoids at 0.39 to 0.99. No shell of any form was measured at Vc 0.9 to 2. Verdict: as a sphere, both leads are beyond the record. 021's 0.595 is 2.5 to 3.3 times it and 021b's 0.468 is 2.0 to 2.6 times, against the S-II hemispheres and against SBKF carried on the handbook sphere-to-cylinder ratio of 0.30 to 0.34. As a cylinder, 021b is at the edge (the pre-1969 record gives about 0.46 at its R/rho, and it sits on SP-8007), while 021 is beyond the pre-1969 record (about 0.43, so 1.39 times) and at the edge of SBKF scaled (0.54 to 0.65). Only a direct cylinder-to-sphere transfer, which no source supports, puts them inside. The best results needed AFP or autoclave faces on stiff honeycomb and measured, modelled shape. 029's FE is the instrument; the record cannot settle Vc 1. Every value is QUESTIONABLE; nothing here is a certification.
